questions.title: DOM & Events practice 1
questions.prompt: What can `querySelector` return when no element matches?
choices: null
An empty string
false only
A new element
questions.explanation: The method returns null when it cannot find a matching element, so code should check before accessing properties.

questions.title: DOM & Events practice 2
questions.prompt: When does a click listener run?
choices: After the registered element receives a click
As soon as it is registered
Before the page loads every time
Only when the function returns text
questions.explanation: Registration stores the callback for later; the browser invokes it when the matching click event occurs.

questions.title: Trace DOM & Events
questions.prompt: What output does this code produce? Enter each line in order.
accepted: The displayed number increases after each click.
questions.explanation: The setup registers one listener. Each click then updates the stored count and the page text. The resulting output is 'The displayed number increases after each click.'.

questions.title: DOM & Events practice 5
choices: querySelector returns null when nothing matches, and reading null.textContent throws
textContent is read-only and cannot be assigned
querySelector returns an array that must be indexed
The guard makes the selector run faster
questions.explanation: When no element matches, `querySelector` returns `null`, and `null.textContent = ...` throws a TypeError. The guard runs the assignment only when an element was found. `querySelector` returns a single element (not an array), `textContent` is writable, and the check is about safety, not speed.

questions.title: DOM & Events concept check 1
questions.prompt: When should JavaScript code prefer `textContent` over `innerHTML`?
choices: `innerHTML` asks the browser to parse markup. Use `textContent` for ordinary user-facing text, especially when a value came from input, so text is displayed rather than treated as page structure.
Use `innerHTML` for untrusted plain text.
Assume a selector always finds an element.
Put a long unrelated workflow inside one event listener.
questions.explanation: `innerHTML` asks the browser to parse markup. Use `textContent` for ordinary user-facing text, especially when a value came from input, so text is displayed rather than treated as page structure. This matters because DOM code connects JavaScript to page elements, so selector checks and safe text updates matter before event code grows.

questions.title: DOM & Events concept check 2
questions.prompt: Which choice describes a reliable DOM & Events practice?
choices: Attach listeners before the relevant element exists.
Select the intended element precisely.
Update the page without checking which event fired.
Use the same id on several elements.
questions.explanation: Select the intended element precisely. This matters because DOM code connects JavaScript to page elements, so selector checks and safe text updates matter before event code grows.

questions.title: DOM & Events concept check 3
questions.prompt: Which DOM & Events code review note is accurate?
choices: Read input values once and never update them.
Ignore event default behavior when it matters.
Check a selector result before use.
Change classes by rewriting the whole class string blindly.
questions.explanation: Check a selector result before use. This matters because DOM code connects JavaScript to page elements, so selector checks and safe text updates matter before event code grows.

questions.title: DOM & Events concept check 4
questions.prompt: Which DOM & Events habit prevents a common mistake?
choices: Store application state only in visible text.
Create elements without attaching them to the page.
Use DOM code for logic that could be tested separately.
Keep listeners short and focused.
questions.explanation: Keep listeners short and focused. This matters because DOM code connects JavaScript to page elements, so selector checks and safe text updates matter before event code grows.

questions.title: DOM & Events concept check 5
questions.prompt: Which DOM & Events advice is accurate?
choices: Display untrusted text with textContent.
Assume every click target is the element with the listener.
Forget to remove listeners created for temporary UI.
Use text parsing to recover data already stored in state.
questions.explanation: Display untrusted text with textContent. This matters because DOM code connects JavaScript to page elements, so selector checks and safe text updates matter before event code grows.

questions.title: DOM & Events concept check 6
questions.prompt: Which statement is accurate about DOM & Events?
choices: Trust user-provided HTML as safe markup.
Connect JavaScript behavior to page elements and user actions.
Run the same listener setup repeatedly.
Hide failures when an element lookup returns null.
questions.explanation: Connect JavaScript behavior to page elements and user actions. This matters because DOM code connects JavaScript to page elements, so selector checks and safe text updates matter before event code grows.
